one_line: Jain mathematician of the Rashtrakuta court, author of the Ganita Sara Sangraha in 9th‑century Manyakheta.

appearance.age_look: Mid-40s, lean and calm scholar’s build.
appearance.face: Oval face, warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed black moustache and short beard along the jaw, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes with a gentle, focused gaze, default expression quietly intent and slightly curious.
appearance.hair: Straight black hair, oiled and combed back into a small low knot at the back of the head; front hair smooth with no fringe; a simple white Jain-style cloth headband encircles the crown, tied discreetly at the back.
appearance.costume: He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton angarakha-style tunic wrapped and tied to the right, with a subtle woven border in muted maroon; below, a soft cotton dhoti in pale cream wrapped from the waist to the ankles in the southern Deccan style, pleats falling in front; over his left shoulder and around the torso is a light, finely woven saffron-tinged ochre cotton uttarīya, its edges line-decorated with thin dark brown stripes; simple brown leather sandals on his feet, and on his wrists plain copper bangles, with a small wooden beaded mala looped around his left wrist to hint at Jain devotional practice.
appearance.signature: A rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Ganita Sara Sangraha, tied with a thin cord and held in his left hand, with a smooth dark wooden stylus held delicately in his right hand as if poised to inscribe calculations.

ref_desc: Mahāvīrācārya is a mid-40s Jain scholar with an oval medium-brown face, black hair in a low knot and white headband, wearing an off-white angarakha, cream dhoti, ochre uttarīya, copper bangles and sandals, holding a palm-leaf manuscript and wooden stylus in ochre-maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Mahāvīrācārya as a dignified 9th-century Jain mathematician from the Deccan: mid-40s, lean, medium-brown skin, oval thoughtful face with straight nose, neatly trimmed black moustache and short beard, and calm, focused almond eyes. His black hair is oiled and combed back into a small low knot at the back of his head, encircled by a simple white cloth headband tied at the back. He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton angarakha-style tunic wrapped and tied to the right with a subtle maroon woven border, a pale cream cotton dhoti wrapped from waist to ankles with frontal pleats in southern style, and a light ochre cotton uttarīya draped from his left shoulder across the torso, edged with thin dark brown stripes. Add plain copper bangles on his wrists, a small wooden beaded mala looped around his left wrist, and simple brown leather sandals. In his left hand he carries a rectangular bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied with a cord, and in his right hand a smooth dark wooden stylus poised as if ready to write. Use a restrained palette of off-white, cream, ochre, maroon, and brown, and present him front-facing in a neutral stance, clearly showing face, hairstyle, garments, sandals, and his manuscript-and-stylus scholarly tools.
